prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.15
  tan: 0.85
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_E:
The Conservatives invite Britons to join a new kind of government built on the belief that we’re all in this together. Britain’s challenges—debt, social breakdown, and a discredited politics—won’t be solved by big government, but by a Big Society: responsibility shared by individuals, families, businesses and communities, with power devolved from the centre.

Core values and approach
- Responsibility: sound public finances, personal responsibility, social responsibility.
- Enterprise and aspiration: a modern, greener, innovative economy.
- Society is not the state: decentralise power to people, professionals and places.
- Progressive Conservatism: equal opportunity, fighting poverty and inequality, improving wellbeing by trusting people and reforming the state.

Fix the economy
- Eliminate the bulk of the structural deficit in a Parliament; create the Office for Budget Responsibility; emergency Budget; £6bn immediate waste cuts; public sector pay freeze (protecting the lowest paid); stop Labour’s “jobs tax” (NI rise) by cutting waste.
- Lower and simplify business taxes (cut corporation tax), reduce regulation, make Britain open for business.
- Rebalance toward saving, investment, exports and hi‑tech leadership (back R&D, STEM, Dyson reforms).
- Welfare-to-work: a single, payment-by-results Work Programme; reassess incapacity claims; sanctions for refusing work; help entrepreneurs and SMEs win procurement.
- Managed immigration: annual cap on non‑EU economic migrants; tighter student visas; promote integration.
- Modern infrastructure: begin high-speed rail; better, not bigger, Heathrow; rail reform; superfast broadband without a phone tax; local enterprise partnerships.

Better public services and safer finance
- Empower professionals and users: transparency (publish spending), payment by results, mutuals and co‑ops to run services.
- Banking reform: bank levy; Bank of England to supervise prudentially; curb risky trading; boost SME credit.

Build a greener economy
- Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; shift taxes toward environmental goals; Green Deal to cut home energy bills; smart grid, offshore wind, CCS; nuclear with no subsidy.

Mend our broken society
- Family-friendly Britain: recognise marriage and civil partnerships in tax; end the couple penalty via welfare reform; council tax freeze; flexible working and shared parental leave; protect childhood from commercial pressures; refocus Sure Start on early intervention; 4,200 more health visitors.
- NHS: protect real-terms funding; patient choice across qualified providers; GP commissioning; scrap non‑clinical targets; publish outcomes; 24/7 urgent care; Cancer Drugs Fund; personal health and care budgets; voluntary insurance option for social care.
- Schools: higher teaching standards and discipline; rigorous curriculum and phonics; technical academies; pupil premium; free schools/expanded academies; protect special schools.

Fight crime and strengthen borders
- Tougher knife sentences; overhaul alcohol licensing; elected police commissioners; cut police paperwork; monthly local crime data; Border Police Force; payment-by-results rehabilitation.

Clean up politics and restore liberties
- Recall MPs; cut number of MPs and ministers’ pay; equalise constituencies; petitions to trigger debates; kill the quango state; radical transparency.
- Protect freedoms: scrap ID cards and databases; curb surveillance and DNA retention; UK Bill of Rights; strengthen data protection.
- Localism: neighbourhood planning, referendums, community right to buy, elected mayors.

Protect the environment
- Conserve habitats, reform fisheries, plant a million trees; honest food labelling; sustainable, high‑welfare farming; science-led badger control for bTB.

Promote our national interest
- National Security Council; succeed in Afghanistan; renew Trident; reform defence procurement; restore the Military Covenant.
- Liberal Conservative foreign policy: champion rights and democracy; strong NATO and US ties; deepen links with India and others; stand firm on Iran; two‑state solution.
- EU: positive but guarded—no more power without a referendum; Sovereignty Bill; repatriate powers on key areas; never join the Euro without a referendum.
- One World Conservatism: honour 0.7% aid by 2013; full transparency and results focus; prioritise the poorest; £500m a year to fight malaria; promote trade-led development.

TEXT_D:
Change that Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain (Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010)

Core purpose: hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing power — economic, social, political and financial — away from vested interests and towards citizens. After decades of red–blue, blue–red governments, the Liberal Democrats offer fundamental reform built around four priorities:

1) Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- Raise the personal allowance to £10,000, a £700 tax cut for most workers; 3.6m low earners and pensioners lifted out of income tax.
- Paid for by: taxing capital gains at income rates; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; replacing Air Passenger Duty with a fairer per‑plane duty (higher for non‑lifeline domestic flights); robust anti‑avoidance and anti‑evasion action; reform of non‑dom status.
- Credible deficit reduction: over £15bn identified savings (e.g., scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; banking levy; cap public‑sector pay rises at £400 for two years; prison reform; reduce quangos; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B). No like‑for‑like Trident replacement; Council on Financial Stability to guide the pace of cuts.

2) A fair chance for every child
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition for disadvantaged pupils; earlier SEN assessment and better teacher training.
- Free schools to innovate: an Education Freedom Act; independent Educational Standards Authority; a slimmer core curriculum; reform league tables.
- Transform 14–19 pathways: a General Diploma to combine academic and vocational learning; FE parity; right to study at college from 14.
- Scrap unfair university tuition fees, phased over six years (final‑year fees ended immediately); targeted national bursaries.

3) A fair future: jobs and green growth
- Break up the banks, separate retail from investment, reform bonuses, and create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- A UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private finance for clean energy and transport.
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 Eco Cash‑Back; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage; major youth work‑experience offer.
- Climate leadership: zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% clean electricity by 2020 (prioritising marine/offshore); home insulation up to £10,000 per home; no new coal without top‑tier CCS; reject new nuclear in favour of cheaper conservation/renewables; build a European Supergrid.
- Transport fairness: shift funding from roads to rail; cut regulated rail fares 1% below inflation annually; regulate buses locally; cancel Heathrow R3; per‑plane duty; plan for fair, revenue‑neutral road pricing later.

4) A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties
- End safe seats with fair votes (STV) and cut 150 MPs; fixed‑term parliaments; a fully elected, smaller second chamber; a written constitution via a citizens’ convention.
- Cleaner politics: recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; statutory lobbyist register; all candidates and parliamentarians tax‑resident in the UK.
- Freedom Bill: roll back the surveillance state; regulate CCTV; protect trial by jury and free speech; end blanket retention of innocent people’s DNA; scrap ID cards; stop unfair US extraditions.

Public services and communities built on fairness
- NHS: cut waste, not care; protect frontline (cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia); integrate health and social care; prevention first; patient entitlements over targets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access.
- Families: shared parental leave; flexible working for all; end child detention in immigration; stronger youth services; equal minimum wage from 16; carers’ respite.
- Older people: restore the earnings link (triple lock: earnings, prices or 2.5%); scrap compulsory retirement ages; long‑term plan for a Citizen’s Pension.
- Crime: 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; empower elected police authorities; target what works, including restorative justice; presumption against short prison sentences; evidence‑based drugs policy.
- Immigration: firm and fair — reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points system; enforce against rogue employers; earned citizenship for long‑settled families pre‑2010; humane, independent asylum system with right to work.
- Pro‑Europe, internationalist and principled abroad: lead EU climate ambition and financial reform; aid at 0.7% of GNI by 2013; defence review; fair pay/housing for forces; no like‑for‑like Trident; uphold human rights, end complicity in torture; two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade.

If you want real, lasting change that works for you, choose fairness: choose the Liberal Democrats.
